Commentary.Commentary: The Afghans would be disappointed but do not forget that this is a semi-final and they have the runs on the board. Only four batsmen managed double figures, which means that the pitch is not the easiest to bat on. Ikram Ali Khil played superbly for his 80 and his drop on 37 might prove the costliest for Australia. Join us back at 1445 local (0145 GMT) for the run chase.

The bowling was good but the fielding was way below par for Australia. They conceded 20 extras, of which, 9 were wides while 5 were penalty runs. Then they dropped a few catches as well and missed run out and stumping opportunities, meaning, Afghanistan could have been restricted to well under 150.

After electing to field, the Aussies did not start all that well, but managed to keep the run flow in check. They were rewarded with wickets eventually and they kept chipping in at regular intervals. It was the pacers' day today as Lloyd Pope got hammered. Jonathan Merlo was the one who put the Afghans under pressure, picking up 4 wickets.

Ryan Hadley is being interviewed by Ian Bishop. He says that it is Australia's best performance so far. Feels that 181 is a par score. Wants the batsmen to bat sensibly and knock off the runs as sometimes quick wickets dent small chases like these. Further says that it is going to be an even contest. On Lloyd Pope's failure today, he says that it happens to everyone.

Australia are happy but that is more because they have just escaped the over-rate punishment. They were threatening to take the innings beyond the scheduled close but some quick wickets towards the end aided their cause. However, they will be happy that they have restricted Afghanistan to 181, albeit the bigger question will be - can the batsmen play spin and chase down 182?

The umpire does not signal anything but walks towards his partner, has a discussion, then refers it upstairs with the soft signal as OUT. The third umpire has a look, sees the deflection on the first replay, then after a couple of other replays is convinced that the keeper Baxter Holt has taken that cleanly. So the drop on 6 not proving too big for Australia in terms of numbers but had that been taken then, the middle order would have been exposed to the swinging ball.

We are done with the national anthems and play is set to begin. Out walk the two Afghan openers - Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran. Ryan Hadley to start off proceedings with the first new ball to Gurbaz. Here we go...
A minute's silence is observed as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the attack in Kabul. Now, it is time for the national anthems. Afghanistan first.

Pitch report - Anjum Chopra says that it is a surprising decision to bat first with overcast skies and a damp wicket. Says the mindset has forced Afghanistan to bat - put runs on the board and defend.

Australian skipper, Jason Sangha says that he was looking to bowl first, so the toss works well for them. The pitch might do well early on, he adds, so hopes the bowlers are up for the task. Adds that the preparation has been very nice coming into the tournament. He too, says that his team is unchanged from the previous game.

Afghanistan captain, Naveen-ul Haq says they would like to bat and put up a score. Adds the track looks good and will do something for the seamers but is confident that they can put up a good score and restrict Australia with their spinners. Informs that they are going in with the same side that beat New Zealand.
TOSS - Time for the toss. Up goes the coin. Heads is the call from Naveen-ul-Haq and Heads it is. AFGHANISTAN CHASE TO BAT.

We are into the final four of the Under-19 World Cup, 2018. Afghanistan and Australia clash today while tomorrow, we would witness the second semi-final between one of the biggest arch rivals in cricket - India and Pakistan. The Aussies entered the semis on the basis of a 8-wicket miracle from Lloyd Pope while Afghanistan have just eased through after crushing New Zealand. Interesting surface on offer.
